judgments.comparative_verdict: Both reports hit all four expectations with correct file/line citations; Report 1 is marginally more thorough (explicit migration chain and cleaner category-(d) removal), but they are essentially comparable.

report_1.evidence: `infra/prod/app.auto.tfvars:2` — `ENABLE_DEBUG_TOOLBAR = "true"`... **Delete the line entirely**... `infra/prod/app.auto.tfvars:4` — `PRESET_ADMIN_ACCOUNTS = "qa@example.com:superadmin"`... **Delete the line entirely.**... `SHADOW_SCORING_SINK = "s3://medislot-shadow/staging/observations/"`... **Delete both lines entirely**... `LEGACY_BILLING_SECRET_ARN`... **Delete the line**

report_2.evidence: `infra/prod/app.auto.tfvars` line 2 — `ENABLE_DEBUG_TOOLBAR = "true"`... Change to `"false"` or remove the key... line 4 — `PRESET_ADMIN_ACCOUNTS = "qa@example.com:superadmin"`... Change to `""` or remove entirely... `SHADOW_SCORING_SINK`... Change to `""` for launch

report_1.evidence: The app reads its API base URL from `import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE_URL` **at build time**... deploy-prod` then deploys **the exact same digest** to prod... the production frontend, as configured, would ship a bundle whose API base URL is `https://staging-api.example.com`... Production needs its own env file (or CI-injected variable), its own build

report_2.evidence: VITE_-prefixed variables are **inlined into the built bundle at build time**... The `deploy-prod` job... deploys **the same already-built digest**... the API base URL in the bundle production users receive is `https://staging-api.example.com`... the fix is either runtime injection of the API base URL... or a separate production build using `--mode production`

report_1.evidence: Nothing runs database migrations. The workflow contains no migration step... the runbook's claim that "Database migrations are applied automatically during deploy"... is unverifiable-at-best... The first production release must apply the full chain `0001_base` → `0002_tenants` → `0003_billing`... to a brand-new, empty prod database; as things stand nothing will.

report_2.evidence: Migrations for an empty prod database are unverifiable. The runbook claims migrations run automatically during deploy, presumably inside the missing `deploy.sh`; the three migrations (`backend/migrations/versions/0001_base.py`–`0003_billing.py`) would all need to run against a brand-new prod database, and nothing in the repo provisions that database

report_1.evidence: the production Terraform passes the **staging** condition into the prod deploy role: `oidc_sub_condition = "repo:acme-health/medislot:environment:staging"` (`infra/prod/main.tf:3`, unchanged from the staging copy)... The fix is a production-scoped condition (`repo:acme-health/medislot:environment:production`)

report_2.evidence: `infra/prod/main.tf:3` — copied unedited from staging — trusts `repo:acme-health/medislot:environment:staging`... **any job running in the staging GitHub environment could assume the production deploy role**... The fix is changing `infra/prod/main.tf:3` to `repo:acme-health/medislot:environment:production`.
